title: Data Wrangling and Profiling
summary: A statistical summary gives information about the data in a sample. It may help with a more thorough understanding of the values. It may include a set of data's mean and standard deviation in addition to the total number of values, lowest value, and greatest value. This aids in understanding the distribution of values, patterns, and outliers within a data set. Better data analysis may result from this, which is especially useful when dealing with large amounts of data.

📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

Data Wrangling Core Definition

Data Wrangling the process in which raw data is converted to a more usable form, which can be used for analysis readily.

Basic Concepts Key Concept

Data wrangling and profiling are the first steps of data analysis process.

Definition Key Concept

Data wrangling is the process in which raw data is converted to a more usable form, which can be used for analysis readily.

Need Of Data Wrangling Key Concept

The relevance of data wrangling continues to grow for several reasons: 1.

Process Of Data Wrangling Key Concept

Data wrangling involves several steps to convert raw data into a form which can be readily used.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

1.2 Basic Concepts

  • Data wrangling and profiling are the first steps of data analysis process.
  • It is performed to enhance data quality and accuracy, resulting in better analysis.
  • Let us first define the two terms used in this unit - Data Wrangling and Profiling in the next sub-section.
  • Definition Data wrangling is the process in which raw data is converted to a more usable form, which can be used for analysis readily.

1.2.1 Definition

  • Data wrangling is the process in which raw data is converted to a more usable form, which can be used for analysis readily.
  • Data Wrangling is also known as Data munging.
  • Data Profiling: Data types, formats, value distributions, patterns, and their interactions, etc., are better understood through this approach.
  • Raw data often has lot of errors, is not accessible for every row and column of the data (missing values), and sometimes is not in an easily usable format.

1.2.2 Need of Data Wrangling

  • The relevance of data wrangling continues to grow for several reasons: 1.
  • Volume, type and variety of Data: Data generation volume has increased multi fold by the evolution of social media, the internet, IoT devices, and many other sources must be appropriately managed and analysed by organisations.
  • Data wrangling enables efficient handling of this exponentially massive and heterogeneous data.
  • Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence: The advancements in analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) require high-quality data.

1.3 Process of Data Wrangling

  • Data wrangling involves several steps to convert raw data into a form which can be readily used.
  • Following steps show how data wrangling works: 1.
  • Collection First step in data wrangling is collecting required data from several sources.
  • These sources include files, databases, IoT device data input, data extraction from websites, and numerous other data streams.

1.4 Benefits of Data Wrangling

  • Data wrangling has numerous advantages that significantly increase the worth of data for companies and organisations.
  • Data wrangling opens the door to more accurate, effective, and insightful research by transforming unstructured data into more structured and clean format.
  • Inaccuracies, inconsistencies, missing values, and repetitions are common in raw data, which can skew analysis and can lead to inaccurate conclusions.
  • To solve these problems, the data wrangling process - cleaning is used, and later the validation step assures that the accurate, consistent and reliable data is used in the analysis.

1.5 Data Semantics

  • Data Semantics represents the meaning and structure of data.
  • By transforming unstructured, confusing data into information with a common meaning, it helps you enforce data integrity and data integration and enhances data analysis.
  • Semantic data models can be produced via an abstraction process that selects real-world data elements and creates links between these attributes to generate organised, meaningful data.
  • Additionally, metadata—data about data—is frequently poorly defined.

1.5.1 Data Semantic Process

  • The following example shows the basic steps that may be used in data semantic process Example: 1.
  • Data Collection: Raw data is gathered from sources.
  • For example, the following raw data may be obtained as a series of data bytes: Name | Value A | 25 B | 30 2.
  • The first record of the raw data, as shown in point 1 above, is organised as JSON object as: { "person": "A", "value": 25 } 15 Introduction to Data Wrangling It is still unclear what “person” and "value" means.

1.5.2 Semantic Wrangling using Data Abstraction

  • Sometimes the available data may need to be generalised or aggregated into different categories.
  • In such situations, you may use data abstraction terms like "is a" (generalisation), "has a" (aggregation), and "instance of" (classification) to perform semantic wrangling.
  • The following semantic relationships describe the connections between the attributes: o Generalisation (Is A): For example, a manager "is a" type of employee.
  • You can establish generalisation ("is a") for a more general object.
